topics.title: Vectors
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Describe position vectors geometrically and as column vectors. (k, u)
Find the vector of a directed line segment when position vectors of the end points are known. (u)
Find the position vector of the mid-point of a line segment. (u)
Use vector method to divide a line proportionately internally and externally. (u, s)
Use vectors to show parallelism. (u, s)
Use vector methods to show co-linearity. (u, s)

body.text: A position vector describes a point's location relative to a fixed origin O. If A is the point (2, 7), its position vector is written OA = (2, 7). The vector from one point to another (e.g. AB) is found by subtracting position vectors: AB = OB - OA.
A is (1, 7) and B is (-3, -3). The vector AB = OB - OA = (-3-1, -3-7) = (-4, -10). The midpoint M of AB has position vector equal to the average of the two: M = ((1+(-3))/2, (7+(-3))/2) = (-1, 2).

Two vectors are parallel if one is a scalar multiple of the other (e.g. (2,4) is parallel to (1,2), since (2,4) = 2x(1,2)). Points are collinear (lie on the same straight line) if the vector between any two of them is parallel to the vector between another two — showing AB and BC are scalar multiples of each other proves A, B and C lie on one line.
